overview:
CA-23 covers the high desert and mountain communities of San Bernardino County and leans Republican by about nine points. Republican Jay Obernolte, the incumbent, advanced to the general election with a decisive financial edge, raising roughly $1.8 million and holding about $1.4 million on hand. Democrat Tessa Lynn Hodge has raised about $123,000 and had only around $17,000 in cash on hand.

No public polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so expectations rest on district partisanship, incumbency, and the money gap. Prediction markets give Obernolte roughly a 98 percent chance of winning. A favorable national environment for Democrats could trim the margin, but the challenger's limited resources make a genuinely competitive contest difficult to see. Obernolte remains the clear favorite to return to Congress.
